source_text: Paternus proconsul dixit: Non solum de episcopis , verum etiam de presbyteris mihi scribere dignati sunt. volo ergo scire ex te qui sint presbyteri qui in hac civitate consistunt. Cyprianus episcopus respondit: Legibus vestris bene atque utiliter censuistis delatores non esse. itaque detegi et deferri a me non possunt. in civitatibus autem suis invenientur. Paternus proconsul dixit: Ego hodie in hoc loco exquiro. Cyprianus dixit: Cum disciplina prohibeat ut quis se ultro offerat, et tuae quoque censurae hoc displiceat, nec offerre se ipsi possunt; sed a te exquisiti invenientur. Paternus proconsul dixit: A me invenientur. et adiecit: Praeceperunt etiam ne in aliquibus locis conciliabula fiant nec coemeteria ingrediantur. si quis itaque hoc tam salubre praeceptum non observaverit, capite plectetur. Cyprianus episcopus respondit: Fac quod tibi praeceptum est.
pass_a_gloss: The proconsul Paternus said they have deigned to write to me not only concerning bishops but also concerning presbyters, so I want to learn from you who the presbyters are who reside in this city. Bishop Cyprian answered that by your own laws you have voted well and usefully that there should be no informers, and therefore they cannot be uncovered and denounced by me, but they will be found in their own cities. Paternus said he is seeking them today in this place. Cyprian said since discipline forbids anyone to offer himself voluntarily, and this is also displeasing to your own judgment, they cannot offer themselves, but when sought out by you they will be found. Paternus said they will be found by me, and he added that they have also ordered that meetings not be held in any places nor cemeteries entered, and so if anyone does not observe this most salutary order he will be punished by death. Bishop Cyprian answered to do what has been ordered to you.
pass_b_english: The proconsul Paternus said, They have deigned to write to me not only about the bishops, but also about the presbyters, and so I wish to learn from you who the presbyters are who remain in this city.

Cyprian the bishop answered, By your own laws you have ordered, well and wisely, that there are to be no informers, and therefore they cannot be uncovered and denounced by me, but they will be found in their own cities.
The proconsul Paternus said, I am seeking them today in this place.

Cyprian said, Since discipline forbids anyone to offer himself of his own accord, and this too offends your own judgment, they cannot offer themselves, but when they are sought by you they will be found.
The proconsul Paternus said, They will be found by me.

And he added, They have also commanded that assemblies be held in no places and that cemeteries be not entered, and so if anyone does not observe this most salutary order, he shall suffer death by the sword.
Cyprian the bishop answered, Do what has been commanded to you.

lemmas.gloss: Roman governor judging the case here
have deigned, formal notice from authority
will be punished, here by beheading

choices.english: that there are to be no informers
choices.why: accusative-infinitive after censuistis states a legal rule, not a past fact, so it renders a standing prohibition
ironic official language in Paternus mouth is kept as praise-form, since salubre modifies praeceptum directly

choices.english: shall suffer death by the sword
choices.why: ablative capite with passive plectetur denotes capital punishment by beheading in judicial idiom
rejected: shall be struck on the head
